newsitem.title: KENYA: Heavy buying pressure builds up at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Heavy buying pressure builds up at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Heavy buying pressure from small investors at the Nairobi Stock Exchange pushed its 20-share index up 56.51 points to 3336.01 on Wednesday, bourse officials said.
Turnover eased to 18.398 million shillings traded on 477,172 shares from 21.649 million shillings traded on 384,363 shares.
"Strong opening prices of index-linked shares drove the index up," one bourse official said.
A senior broker said the flood of investors into the market was because they wanted to catch prices at their current levels before the upswing pushed them too high.
Uchumi Supermarket, currently trading cum-bonus, jumped to 60 from 55 driven by demand for bonus issue shares before the closing date of February 3.
Financials traded heavily with Barclays Bank gaining 3.0 to close at 116, while Standard Chartered Bank was at 56 unchanged.
Foreigners bought 40,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at 83-85 from 82 and 18,700 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee at 65 from 64.50.
Brokers said the low turnover reflected the fact that bourse investors were holders for the long term rather than the short term.
The NSE's current average market turnover stands at 3.0 percent.
Kenya Airways continued edging towards what brokers said was its fair market value, closing at 10 from 9.75.
Kenya Oil Company traded at 63 from 56.50, while Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 174 from 176.
